correctness.rationale: The exact hyperplane shadow of an extruded Euclidean ball is a swept (d-1)-ball with brightness kappa_(d-1)+2t kappa_(d-2) sin(theta). This determines the projection body as an n-ball plus a flat disk. Axial integration yields the Bernstein coefficients, whose first adjacent ratio is one by the ball slicing identities and later ratios exceed one by strict Holder/Cauchy-Schwarz log-convexity. Hence the Bernstein derivative is strictly positive for every finite positive t and every d>=3. The limiting coefficients and affine covariance follow. A standalone verifier completed 214 supplementary checks, which do not replace the proof.
